content:
Hello everyone, I'm thinking of formalizing the categorical fixed-point calculus in Lean. Do you think this would be a welcome contribution to mathlib?

The categorical fixed point calculus is a collection of theorems about initial algebras of endofunctors. When endofunctors model datatypes, their initial algebras represent recursive structures and the calculus gives isomorphisms that can be used to reshape recursive data. As far as I can tell, mathlib already has all the category-theoretic definitions, (up to endofunctors and the category of F-algebras) and goes as far as considering an initial object and proving Lambek's lemma, Algebra.Initial.str_isIso, but doesn't have the other theorems, like the rolling rule or the square rule. There are also some theorems in Order.FixedPoints that are direct corollaries of the categorical calculus (when one takes the underlying category to be a complete lattice), like map_lfp_comp and lfp_lfp.

I'm somewhat familiar with the material and was thinking that this might be an interesting first real formalization project. The book "Mathematics of Program Construction" by Roland Backhouse has a section on the calculus which I'd use as a main reference. I'll also add that I'm not interested in using AI to generate code because it would somewhat defeat my learning objective.

Would this be a valuable contribution to the library? Any pointers to related formalization projects are also appreciated.

There was a previous attempt at formalizing this using AI, which is the reason it was not added to mathlib. If you want to learn the Lean language and formalize this result, this could be a nice addition to mathlib.
